relations.subject: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
relations.evidence: Ishwar Chandra joined the Sanskrit College, Calcutta, and studied there for twelve long years and graduated in 1841

relations.subject: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
relations.evidence: In 1841, at the age of twenty-one years, Ishwar Chandra joined Fort William College as head of the Sanskrit department. After five years, in 1846, Vidyasagar left Fort William College

relations.subject: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
relations.evidence: in 1846, Vidyasagar left Fort William College and joined the Sanskrit College as 'Assistant Secretary'.... In 1849, against the advice of Rasomoy Dutta, he resigned from Sanskrit College

relations.subject: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
relations.evidence: In 1849, against the advice of Rasomoy Dutta, he resigned from Sanskrit College and rejoined Fort William College as a head clerk.

relations.subject: Dwarakanath Vidyabhusan
relations.evidence: Dwarakanath (1819–1886) was a professor of the Sanskrit College in Calcutta, India.

relations.subject: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
relations.evidence: A weekly newspaper, Somprakash Patrika, was started on 15 November 1858... by Dwarakanath Vidyabhusan.... The original plan was mooted by Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar... who continued to advise Dwarakanath

relations.subject: Rasomoy Dutta
relations.evidence: This report resulted in a serious altercation between Ishwar Chandra and College Secretary Rasomoy Dutta.
